correctness.rationale: A matching after at most one new edge exists exactly if at least three distinct units survive and survivors occur in at least two of the three original classes. The converse selects one survivor from each of two represented plants and a third distinct survivor to serve the missing plant via its only new edge; if all three represented, original edges suffice. Subtract disjoint one-class-survivor events from Bin(n,p)>=3 to derive exact R=C_n−ΣG(m_i). Direct Pascal differences yield Δ²G(m)=p²q^(n−m−2)(1−q^m)>0, hence strict balancing by integer transfers and unique balanced multiset. G(m)=0 iff m<=2, so physical ideal C_n attainable iff n<=6, with first gap p³q⁴ at n=7. Independently enumerated survival masks and used an equivalent but separate represented-class criterion for all n 3..8 compositions and p=1/4,1/2.

value.rationale: Post-failure recourse can invalidate naive static redundancy designs; the theorem identifies the exact stochastic event and proves a nontrivial all-n, all-p unique optimum, with the sharp six-to-seven unattainability threshold. The discrete convexity lemma is motivated by and exactly resolves this capacity-constrained matching objective, giving a useful benchmark for reliability theory rather than an arbitrary slice. No empirical conservation success is claimed.

final_claim: For n>=3 independent equal-survival capacity-one specialists assigned to three plants, with one extra link allowed adaptively after failures, full-service reliability is binomial three-survivor probability minus three one-class-tail penalties and is uniquely optimized by class sizes differing at most one; the ideal upper bound is achievable exactly for 3<=n<=6, with n=7 shortfall p^3(1-p)^4.
limitations: Mathematical static capacity-one model only; no ecological field inference, heterogeneous survival, simultaneous adaptive multiple edges, or cost constraints.
